title: Valid Palindrome
interviewTips: Ask what counts as valid: only alphanumeric characters case-insensitive, all other characters ignored
Trade-off to discuss: extra O(n) string for simplicity vs O(1) two-pointer scan for optimal space
Edge-case tip: empty string or string with only non-alphanumerics like '., ' is a valid palindrome

approaches.name: Approach 1: Filter and Reverse
approaches.intuition: First normalize the string by keeping only alphanumeric characters in lowercase, then check if it reads the same forward and backward.
approaches.theory: Build a cleaned string t containing lowercased alphanumerics from s. A string is a palindrome iff t equals reverse(t). This separates cleaning from checking, making logic trivially correct at cost of extra storage for t and its reverse.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass to filter n characters plus O(n) to reverse and compare, linear overall.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Stores filtered string and its reverse, both up to n length in worst case.

dryRunExample.input: s = A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
steps: forward equals reverse so return true

edgeCases: string with only spaces and punctuation like '., ' returns true
single alphanumeric like 'a' or '0P' handling case-insensitivity

approaches.name: Approach 2: Two Pointers with Skipping
approaches.intuition: Compare characters from both ends moving inward, skipping non-alphanumerics on the fly without building a new string.
approaches.theory: Maintain left l at start and right r at end. Advance l past non-alphanumerics and retreat r past non-alphanumerics, then compare lowercased s[l] and s[r]. If any mismatch, not a palindrome. If pointers cross, it is a palindrome. This checks the same filtered sequence implicitly in O(1) extra space.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each character visited at most once by left or right pointer, linear scan.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two indices and constant temporaries, no extra string.

dryRunExample.input: s = A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
steps: l=0 A vs r=29 a -> match, move inward
skip spaces and commas and colon symmetrically
all mirrored pairs m-m, a-a, n-n match until pointers cross -> return true

edgeCases: race a car returns false due to middle mismatch
0P returns false because 0 != p, while empty and punctuation-only return true
